battlecards.why_selected: Lowest total landed cost on corrugate after BAFO; strong savings concentrated in top 5 OpCos (96% of benefit); positive site-visit feedback; willing to hold pricing for 12 months.
battlecards.contract_terms: Initial 2-year MOU with 1-year renewal option; fixed case pricing, quarterly fuel & OCC index review cap ±3%.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Multi-lot RFP with eight bidders, ability to award by lot, bundled volume from multiple OpCos, threat of single-source award to Landsberg.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Significant cost savings; responsive leadership; Midwest footprint aligns with majority of FreshEdge volume.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: No coverage for FL/AL OpCos which will still rely on alternates; corrugate only (no packaging or labels).
battlecards.switching_costs: Die-cut tooling changes and artwork re-approval; transition of inventory (estimated 6-8 weeks).
battlecards.notes: MOU draft circulated 8/5/24; awaiting FreshEdge signature before implementation kick-off.

battlecards.why_selected: Delivered national reach covering all locations for packaging/labels; competitive pricing within 2% of lowest bid; agreed to hold inventory in regional DCs.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year master agreement; price holds for 12 months, then CPI-capped escalator; 30-day out for service failure.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Ability to split award with corrugate lot, packaging/labels could be consolidated; Bunzl keen to expand produce segment footprint.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Broad SKU catalog; proven national logistics; ability to on-board smaller OpCos quickly.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historical service concerns at Get Fresh (customer felt like a 'small fish'); did not bid on corrugate portion.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal—mostly consumables; require SKU cross-reference and system updates.
battlecards.notes: MOU submitted alongside Welch; implementation will run in parallel beginning Q4-24.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Total savings below Welch/Bunzl scenario; only bid partial markets requiring staggered roll-out; labels savings offset by higher corrugate costs.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Kept in mix to pressure primary bidders during BAFO.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: One-stop shop capability across categories; national footprint.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Staggered implementation, higher total cost, limited Indy market coverage.
battlecards.notes: May be approached for contingency supply in FL/AL if Welch coverage gap persists.
complexity_reasons: Used as competitive leverage in BAFO

battlecards.why_selected: Matched target price of $5.99 per pallet; added $1.49 rebate for damaged pallets; met all business requirements except minor audit reporting.
battlecards.contract_terms: 1-year MOU effective 5/1/24 with 12-month fixed pricing and buy-back schedule (Schedule A).
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive quotes from 48Forty & General Pallet; threat of shift of 50% volume.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing depot network, proven service, quick to match pricing, offers rebate program.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial reluctance on internal audit reporting; regional focus (Indy heavy).
battlecards.switching_costs: Would require trailer swaps and new core credit processes if moved.
battlecards.notes: Savings delivered without operational change—decision driven by risk avoidance vs extra $30k with 48Forty.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Additional $30k savings over Kamps not enough to offset switching risk and operational disruption.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used by FreshEdge to obtain concessions from Kamps.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Nationwide coverage, aggressive pricing, scalable capacity.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: No existing relationship; unknown service levels at Indy Fruit.
battlecards.switching_costs: Trailer swap outs, new EDI integration, pallet spec validation.
battlecards.notes: May be re-engaged if Kamps service deteriorates.

battlecards.why_selected: National discount structure through WPP card—simple implementation, consolidated reporting, diesel rebates by tier.
battlecards.contract_terms: Evergreen participation agreement; discounts pegged to OPIS index minus c-per-gallon; 30-day exit.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregate fuel volume (>16 M gallons) across fleet to secure lowest tier rebate.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Large nationwide network, integrated fleet card, simple rollout.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Limited in-ground tank support; credit line approval pending for two smaller OpCos.
battlecards.switching_costs: Card replacement and driver training; modest.
battlecards.notes: Implementation led by WPP contact Felipe; go-live Q3-24.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Higher effective cost per gallon versus WPP tiered discount; limited national footprint.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Used incumbent cost data to benchmark savings with WPP.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Insufficient pricing competitiveness; regional coverage only.
battlecards.switching_costs: Card termination and account closure; no hard assets.
complexity_reasons: Supplier displaced as part of consolidation

alternatives_considered: Staying with Ohio Edison default tariff
battlecards.why_selected: 4-year fixed price mitigates projected 12-17% market increases; highest NPV savings among offers.
battlecards.contract_terms: 48-month fixed-rate supply starting 5/14/2024; utility consolidated billing; early-termination pass-through cost.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive broker process run by Freedom Energy Logistics; timing ahead of expected market rise.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Stable rate, reputable supplier, flexible billing.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Longer commitment term; negative savings in Year 1 (-3%) before hedging benefit materializes.
battlecards.switching_costs: Early term fee if market rates fall; minimal operational impact.
battlecards.notes: Projected cumulative savings $61k over four years; similar gas contract signed with Gas South.
